reasoning: Trump’s removal before 2027 is very unlikely. He is in good health for a 78-year-old, and presidents receive top medical care; actuarial death risk over two years is around 4%, and other removal mechanisms (impeachment, 25th amendment) are politically infeasible given Republican control of Congress and his solid base. Even adding a slim chance for resignation, total probability remains around 4%. The market-implied 9.5% is significantly too high.
evidence_points: Social Security actuarial tables assign about 4% annual mortality for 78-year-old males; presidential healthcare further lowers risk, so ~4% over two years is generous.
Republicans hold the Senate, making conviction in an impeachment trial nearly impossible after a House vote (which itself is unlikely).
No serious health scares or incapacitation events have been reported; the 25th Amendment sustained removal requires broad bipartisan consensus that does not exist.
Resignation under scandal is historically rare for sitting presidents in first two years and would require overwhelming pressure that has not materialized.
sources_consulted: Current political environment and Congressional composition
Public health assessments of Donald Trump
